diagnostics.finding: The induction repeatedly introduces new codimension-one cones, and termination was not established in dimensions at least three. The erratum replaces that argument.

diagnostics.scope: A scalar relation does not preserve the vector target; the separate normal-fan proof of Lemma 2.1 is unaffected.
The relation is now a correct vector relation; zeroing untouched positive coordinates still destroys feasibility. No counterexample to the main proposition is claimed.

diagnostics.corrected: product_i a_{d e_i}^{p_i} subset a_{d m}
diagnostics.witness: In k[x], a_even=R and a_odd=(x), with a_0=R. Its Rees algebra is generated by xt and t^2. For d=2,e=1,p=1,m=1, a_2=R is not contained in a_1=(x), but is contained in a_2. The displayed inequality (7) itself uses the correct degree.
diagnostics.scope: Degree typo in explanatory prose, not failure of the displayed valuation chain.

diagnostics.source: Original Example 1.11, printed p.1708 / physical p.9
diagnostics.witness: On P^2, take D=2H, A=H, E=H and Zariski decomposition P=2H,N=0. The support of E is a line, whereas Null(P) is empty.
diagnostics.scope: The standard surface augmented-base-locus identity is not refuted.

diagnostics.source: Original Definition 2.9, printed p.1716 / physical p.17
diagnostics.printed: Every irreducible subvariety Z of X is the center of a discrete valuation of k(X).
diagnostics.corrected: Specify a nonempty proper irreducible subvariety for a nontrivial rank-one discrete valuation.
diagnostics.witness: If Z=X, the local ring at its generic point is k(X). A valuation ring containing k(X) inside k(X) is the field itself, not a nontrivial discrete valuation ring.
diagnostics.scope: For the big-divisor base-locus applications the relevant centers are proper; no main theorem counterexample is claimed.

diagnostics.source: Original Proposition 3.1 proof, printed p.1719 / physical p.20
diagnostics.scope: The difference is a nonnegative combination of zero-valued basis vectors. Subadditivity gives the needed inequality, and the remaining Lipschitz argument survives.

diagnostics.source: Original Lemma 3.3, printed p.1720 / physical p.21
diagnostics.finding: Its displayed formula is an infimum; the prose calls it a minimum. Preserve the infimum unless attainment has been separately established. The finite-dimensional rational feasible polyhedron in erratum Lemma 2.1 is a different setting where attainment is proved.

diagnostics.source: Original unstable-locus paragraph, printed p.1724 / physical p.25; its own Example 1.27, physical pp.13--14
diagnostics.printed: No isolated rays; no isolated points in any section of the big cone.
diagnostics.witness: For Bl_P(P^2), D=xH-yE and the big cone x>max(y,0), the positive H ray y=0 is the only unstable ray in the big cone, using Example 1.27. In the local section x=1 the unstable point y=0 is isolated.
diagnostics.scope: A boundary in a one-dimensional section can be isolated. The finite-generation theorem and measure-zero conclusion are not refuted.

diagnostics.source: Original moving intersection before (4.3), printed p.1731 / physical p.32
diagnostics.printed: Use a base ideal b != O_X and put (L^[n])=0 when b=O_X.
diagnostics.corrected: Use a nonzero base ideal; put the moving intersection to zero when the base ideal is zero. For b=O_X the moving part is pi^*L.
diagnostics.witness: For L=O(1) on P^1 every multiple is basepoint-free, so the printed rule would make the right side of (4.3) zero, while vol(L)=1.
diagnostics.scope: The zero ideal (no sections) and the unit ideal (basepoint-free series) must be distinguished. No counterexample to Fujita approximation or Proposition 4.13 is claimed.

diagnostics.source: Original Proposition 4.13 proof, printed p.1732 / physical p.33
diagnostics.printed: The ray ideal in (dagger) has subscript p e_i; the quantifier says p in N^n.
diagnostics.corrected: Use a_{d e_i}^{p_i} and p in N^r, consistently with the fixed integer d, the immediately following resolution of a_{d e_i}, and the r grading directions.
diagnostics.scope: An index/dimension typo. Keep integral closure on both sides; principalization depends only on the integral closure of these ideals.
